anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Multiple concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same objects, creating blocking chains or deadlocks that force sessions to wait or be aborted.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Sessions compete for access to hot buffer-pool pages, latches, or I/O slots, stalling while they spin or sleep for low-level synchronization resources.

Composite anomaly definition: The database concurrently suffers from high-level transaction lock contention and low-level buffer/latch contention, so statements are serialized twice—first at the lock manager and again inside the buffer manager—causing severe throughput collapse and runaway latency.

Combined observable phenomena: In addition to long lock-wait queues, deadlock victim errors, and rising application timeouts, the instance also exhibits surges in buffer-busy/page-latch wait events, elevated CPU spin time, and slow physical I/O completions. Wait graphs may show the same sessions alternating between "lock" and "latch/buffer busy" wait states; lock-wait durations appear longer because latch stalls delay lock acquisition and release, while latch contention metrics spike because blocked transactions hold buffer pins longer. Connection pools exhaust, checkpoint and autovacuum tasks fall behind, and overall throughput degrades non-linearly.

Causal interaction: Hot rows or index keys draw many concurrent updates, creating lock hot spots. While blocked, holders keep buffer pages pinned, shrinking the effective buffer-pool supply and funnelling more threads toward the same hot pages, which in turn amplifies latch contention. Conversely, heavy latch or buffer-busy waits slow down the execution and commit phases of transactions, prolonging their lock tenure and enlarging blocker chains or deadlock windows. The two feedback loops reinforce each other: prolonged locks worsen buffer pressure; buffer/latch stalls lengthen lock lifetimes, producing a compounding congestion spiral that can culminate in systemic throughput collapse and widespread query timeouts.

entry.official_description: Minimum record flag is wrongly set to rec on page '%lu' at level '%lu' for index '%s' of table '%s'.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
